hyps.why: At tiny learning rates training is under-converged after 243 epochs, so raising the rate gives large gains compared with elsewhere.
Rates of 0.08 to 1 already make Adam unstable, so going higher causes divergence and sharp accuracy drops.
Lowering an already tiny rate further starves optimization, hurting much more than lowering a moderate or high rate.
Large batches give few update steps, so a higher learning rate compensates and helps more than with small batches.
Small batches already give many noisy updates, so a higher rate tips them into instability.
With a tiny learning rate, the fewer updates from a larger batch leave the network further from convergence.
At high learning rates, larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training, so increasing batch size helps.
Moving alpha from 0.13 toward 1 causes severe underfitting, while changes at small alpha are negligible.
Very narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening already-wide networks.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units at high learning rates, so adding a layer hurts there.
